requirement: Prepare a JSONL input file for the OpenAI Batch API from many chat requests and turn the returned output file into answers and per-request errors.
skeleton: An ENDPOINT constant, a DuplicateCustomIdError, build_batch emitting one request line per unique custom_id with a trailing newline, and read_results splitting records into answers and errors.
caption: Writing and reading OpenAI Batch API JSONL files. build_batch(items, *, model) turns each custom_id and messages pair into a JSON line with method POST, url ENDPOINT /v1/chat/completions and a body holding the model and messages, raising DuplicateCustomIdError, a ValueError quoting the id, when a custom_id repeats. Lines are joined with newlines and end with a trailing newline, and an empty batch is empty text. read_results(text) skips blank lines, parses each record, and files a top-level error message, or the error message from a response whose status_code is not 200, under errors; otherwise it stores the first choice content under answers. The fixture asserts that two requests make two lines ending in a newline with the exact request shape, that an empty batch is empty text, that a repeated a raises DuplicateCustomIdError, and that mixed output with a blank line yields answers a and d and errors bad model and expired.

plan.intent: Run offline evaluations through the Batch API
constraints: Each request has custom_id, method POST, url ENDPOINT and a body
Output ends with a newline and an empty batch is empty text
Top-level errors and non-200 responses are collected as errors

rationale.teaches: Custom ids are the only join key between batch input and output, so enforce uniqueness and handle both error shapes the output file uses.
rationale.why: Duplicate ids make results ambiguous, a wrong url fails every request, and assuming every response succeeded crashes on the first 4xx record.

ops.docstring: Build OpenAI Batch API input files and read their output files.

ops.source:
class DuplicateCustomIdError(ValueError):
    """Raised when two batch requests share one custom_id."""

candidates.why_wrong: Repeated custom ids are written, making batch results ambiguous.
The JSONL file lacks its trailing newline after the last request.
A blank line in the output file crashes JSON parsing.
A non-200 response is read as a success and crashes on missing choices.
Requests target a url the Batch API does not accept.
